title: Decentralized canary + sparse-update flow for verified performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: As we onboard more open model variants and publish Redwood-verified performance profiles, the current bulk publish workflow creates maintenance friction and high operational blast radius. Large profile publishes take time, can invalidate older downstream pinning unexpectedly, and create noisy alerts when minor metric shifts occur.

Goal: Implement a decentralized canary + sparse-update publishing flow for verified performance profiles that: 1) allows incremental (sparse) updates for targeted metrics or model variants, 2) runs automated canaries against representative production traces, and 3) provides deterministic roll-forward/rollback rules plus observability to quantify customer impact.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-level requirements, rollout policy, acceptance criteria, and stakeholder signoffs required to hand the design to ENG (runtime + release infra) and DX (console + docs). Implementation tasks (ENG work) will be tracked in dependent ENG tickets.

Why now: Volume of model variant uploads and small tuning/quantization updates has grown 3x in the last quarter. Manual publishes and full-profile re-signatures are slowing onboarding and increasing the chance of regressing latency/cost for customers who pin older versions. A targeted canary approach enables faster safe publishes and reduces churn in downstream pinning flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Product supports publishing a sparse profile update that targets a specific metric dimension (latency, throughput, or cost) or a subset of model variants without touching other verified fields.
2) Each sparse publish automatically triggers a canary suite using a saved trace set and compares p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M-tokens against the currently pinned profile; delta thresholds are configurable per-project.
3) Canary runs produce a standardized verdict: PASS / WARN / FAIL with quantized deltas and linkable artifacts (raw traces, perf matrices, PR link).
4) For PASS: profile change is auto-promoted to the canonical registry with an immutable signed version and a changelog entry. For WARN: requires product + runtime approval. For FAIL: auto-rollback and open incident flagged to oncall.
5) Console shows a dedicated "Profile Canary" timeline for each publish (start/end time, verdict, key metrics) and a one-click rollback.
6) Upstream consumers (model-pinning APIs) get a notif/preview that indicates whether a new profile is sparse or breaking; pinning decisions preserve backward compatibility unless explicitly forced.
